note: Every room sells exactly eight pieces of its own (`catalogues`, one list per room, in slot order — the position of a piece is the numbered place it stands in, see roomAnchors.ts). A piece is sold in one room only and a room holds each of its pieces once, so the meter is exactly full when the set is in: a room's decorTarget is the sum of its coin pieces. Prices scale with the room — about 60% of the room's own price spread over the eight, dearer for higher-rated guest rooms, gem rooms converted at 10,000 coins a gem. Pieces in no catalogue are built-ins: drawn by the rooms they furnish, never sold. Older catalogue notes:  Two tiers were added to every category reaching levels 38 and 50: the catalogue stopped around level 25 while the progression curve now runs to 60, leaving a player past their first month with one item left to want in the whole game.  Room scope (HC-P1-S5): every piece now names the rooms it belongs in, and 43 pieces were added for the rooms that had nothing of their own — the gym had a treadmill and a weight rack against eight slots, the pool and the cinema had nothing at all, and the back of house shared one cleaning trolley.
